easy.def: A word that shows something is touching the top or side of something.
examples: The cup is on the table.
A bug sat on my arm.
Hang your coat on the hook.

more.def: A word used to show that something rests upon a surface, hangs from something, or happens at a certain time.
examples: The picture hangs on the wall above the piano.
We have a spelling test on Friday.
A tiny frog sat on a lily pad.

easy.def: On a ship, plane or train.
examples: We are onboard now.
The kids went onboard.
Everyone is onboard.

more.def: On or into a ship, plane, train or bus.
examples: The passengers went onboard the ship just before noon.
Once everyone was onboard, the train left the station.
We stepped onboard and found our seats on the plane.

easy.def: Carried on a ship, plane or car.
examples: The onboard snacks are free.
The onboard camera works.
We use the onboard map.

more.def: Found or carried on a vehicle, such as a ship, plane or car.
examples: The plane's onboard computer helps the pilot fly.
We watched an onboard movie on the long flight.
The onboard camera on the boat took pictures of the whales.
I went once.
She sings once a day.
Try it once.

more.def: One time and no more, or at some time in the past.
examples: We visit my grandfather once a month.
I have been to the ocean only once.
A large lake once covered this valley.
I have one nose.
One plus one is two.
She ate one grape.

more.def: The number 1, which is a single thing.
examples: The farmer counted one cow still missing from the field.
A week has seven days, and a day has one sunrise.
There is only one tallest tree in the park.
It is an ongoing game.
The work is ongoing.
An ongoing story.

more.def: Still happening and not yet finished.
examples: The work on the new bridge is ongoing and should end by spring.
We have an ongoing project to learn about birds.
The ongoing rain made the field muddy.

easy.def: A round vegetable with layers that makes you cry.
examples: The onion has layers.
I cut an onion.
The onion made me cry.

more.def: A round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste.
examples: Dad chopped an onion for the soup.
The onion made my eyes water.
Onions grow under the ground.
I am online.
An online game.
The shop is online.

more.def: Connected to the internet, or done over the internet.
examples: I looked it up on an online map.
She plays an online game.
The store has an online shop.

easy.def: A person who watches something happen.
examples: An onlooker watched the game.
The onlookers cheered.
A crowd of onlookers gathered.

more.def: A person who watches something happen without taking part in it.
examples: A crowd of onlookers gathered to watch the street painter.
The onlooker clapped when the parade went by.
The onlookers stood back as the workers lifted the heavy beam.
I have only one pen.
She only wants water.
Only a few came.

more.def: And nothing or no one else, or just that amount.
examples: There is only one flavor of ice cream left.
I only need a minute to finish this drawing.
The shop is open only on weekdays.
The onset of winter.
The onset of rain.
The cold onset came.

more.def: The start of something, often something unpleasant.
examples: The onset of winter brought snow.
We hurried home at the onset of the storm.
The onset of the cold made her sneeze.

easy.def: On the stage where the show is.
examples: She walked onstage.
The band came onstage.
He stood onstage.

more.def: On the stage, where the audience can see you.
examples: The singer walked onstage and the crowd cheered.
The whole class came onstage to bow.
He felt nervous standing onstage in front of everyone.

easy.def: To a place on top of.
examples: The cat jumped onto the bed.
Put the book onto the shelf.
The ball rolled onto the road.

more.def: Moving to a position on the surface of something.
examples: The cat jumped onto the table.
The children climbed onto the stage.
The water spilled onto the floor.
